warnings: cv2.VideoCapture lacks try/finally or context manager; unexpected exceptions during frame reading could leak OS video handles.
pickle.load() used for MoCap data poses arbitrary code execution risk if file integrity is compromised or sourced from untrusted pipelines.
Hardcoded absolute Windows path (ROOT_DIR) reduces portability and will fail in cross-platform deployments or CI/CD environments.
datetime.utcnow() is deprecated in Python 3.12+; may trigger deprecation warnings in newer runtime environments.
Rigid camera naming logic assumes exactly two filename patterns, which may mislabel additional cameras or cause key collisions.
recommendations: Wrap cv2.VideoCapture operations in a try/finally block to guarantee cap.release() is called even if an exception occurs mid-processing.
Replace pickle with JSON, msgpack, or a validated schema-based format for MoCap data to eliminate deserialization security risks.
Externalize directory paths using environment variables or a configuration file (e.g., .env, YAML) instead of hardcoding absolute paths.
Add explicit type validation for analyze_mocap_dynamics return values; currently, error dicts are stored as spatial metrics without clear downstream handling.
Consider streaming/chunked processing or memory-mapped files if MoCap datasets exceed available RAM on the MiR100 edge hardware.
